No immediate complications were observed.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Giant cell tumor of bone (GCTB), Campanacci stage III, left middle finger middle phalanx
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old healthy, active woman presented in January 2017 with a 1-year history of progressive pain, tenderness, and swelling in the left middle finger middle phalanx following minor trauma to the right hand. Physical examination revealed a firm, tender mass at the middle phalanx with preserved adjacent joint motion and normal neurovascular status. Plain radiography demonstrated a geographic osteolytic lesion on the shaft of the middle phalanx with a well-defined sclerotic border and no periosteal reaction. MRI showed a hypointense solid intramedullary lesion with hyperintense surrounding soft tissue, indicating soft tissue extension. At 6-month follow-up, radiography revealed progression with an expansile osteolytic lesion, articular involvement, and cortical extension, with no pulmonary metastasis on chest imaging. Histopathology confirmed giant cell tumor of bone classified as Campanacci stage III. Given the extensive involvement of the middle phalanx with local invasion, middle phalanx resection and interphalangeal joint arthrodesis with iliac bone graft were performed with no immediate complications. At 1-year follow-up, the patient was pain-free with some functional limitation from phalangeal fusion, and plain radiography showed union with no evidence of recurrence.
